question: Should this Claw mission-control backbone land in OpenClaw core as one sponsored product/API surface, be split into narrower repairable slices, or be paused until storage and security architecture are approved?
rationale: The PR is not only a code repair; it creates new core runtime, config, Gateway protocol, UI, docs, workflow, and storage surfaces, so automation cannot safely choose the product boundary or approve exceptions.

options.title: Split and repair first
options.body: Require a clean branch with SQLite-backed state or an explicit storage exception, mission-id validation, preserved HTTP/1 SSRF dispatchers, and real lifecycle proof before any core feature landing.

options.title: Sponsor as one core feature
options.body: A maintainer can explicitly accept the broad Claw core surface after conflicts are resolved and proof demonstrates the end-to-end Gateway plus Control UI workflow.

options.title: Pause this branch
options.body: Close or pause this broad branch and invite narrower PRs for separable browser hardening, runtime plumbing, or UI/docs pieces.

recommendation.title: Split and repair first
recommendation.body: Require a clean branch with SQLite-backed state or an explicit storage exception, mission-id validation, preserved HTTP/1 SSRF dispatchers, and real lifecycle proof before any core feature landing.

likelyOwner.reason: The current blockers span core architecture and security-sensitive networking, and this person is the strongest current-main routing signal from the inspected history.
